guide.title: ECG Basics & the 12-Lead
guide.lead: The 12-lead is the fastest way to open a blocked artery: if you find the STEMI, the cath lab gets ready before you arrive. Know the boxes, place the leads right, read the territories, and know what mimics a STEMI.

sections.title: Chest leads
rows: Anterior / mid-axillary line, level with V4
V4 position on the right chest

sections.title: Territories
notes: STEMI: new ST elevation in 2 contiguous leads, 1 mm (V2–V3: 2 mm men 40 or older, 2.5 mm men under 40, 1.5 mm women).
Reciprocal ST depression supports a STEMI.

groups.title: Treat like STEMI
items: LBBB or paced rhythm with ongoing ischemic symptoms (Sgarbossa)

groups.title: High risk, not STEMI
items: Wellens' T waves: critical LAD narrowing

groups.title: STEMI mimics
items: Pericarditis: diffuse concave ST elevation, PR depression

quiz.q: At 25 mm/s the PR interval is 4 small boxes. Value and normal?
Inferior ST elevation and BP 82/50. Extra lead and drug to avoid?
Ischemic chest pain with LBBB on the 12-lead. Your response?
options: Manage like a STEMI: Sgarbossa criteria help; pre-notify the PCI centre
Ignore: LBBB makes the ECG unreadable
Only if reciprocal changes are present
Not STEMI unless ST elevation exceeds 4 mm
quiz.explanation: LBBB with ongoing ischemic symptoms is a STEMI equivalent.

quiz.q: One small box at 25 mm/s equals:
quiz.explanation: A large box (5 small) is 0.20 s.

quiz.q: Which leads look at the lateral wall?
ST depression in V1–V3 with ongoing chest pain. Next step?
options: Record V7–V9 to look for a posterior MI
Ignore: depression is never a STEMI
quiz.explanation: Posterior MI shows as mirror-image depression in V1–V3.

quiz.q: STEMI threshold in V2–V3 for a woman:
quiz.explanation: Men 40 or older 2 mm; men under 40 2.5 mm; other leads 1 mm.

quiz.q: Diffuse concave ST elevation with PR depression and positional pain suggests:
quiz.explanation: A classic STEMI mimic: still needs hospital assessment.

options: Under the left nipple, wherever it is
quiz.explanation: V5 and V6 sit level with V4.

options: Count the QRS complexes and multiply by 10
Count large boxes and divide by 300

flashcards.question: One large box at 25 mm/s
flashcards.answer: 0.20 s. One small box is 0.04 s.

flashcards.question: Normal PR interval
flashcards.answer: 0.12–0.20 s (3–5 small boxes): SA node through the atria and AV node to the ventricles.

flashcards.question: Standard calibration
flashcards.answer: 10 mm = 1 mV (the square pulse at the start).

flashcards.question: V1 and V2 placement
flashcards.answer: V1: 4th intercostal space, right sternal border. V2: 4th intercostal space, left sternal border.

flashcards.question: STEMI criteria
flashcards.answer: New ST elevation in 2 contiguous leads: 1 mm, except V2–V3 (2 mm men 40 or older, 2.5 mm men under 40, 1.5 mm women).

flashcards.question: Territories
flashcards.answer: Inferior II, III, aVF. Anterior V1–V4. Lateral I, aVL, V5–V6. Posterior: ST depression V1–V3, elevation in V7–V9.

flashcards.question: Three STEMI mimics
flashcards.answer: Pericarditis (diffuse ST elevation, PR depression), early repolarization, LVH. Also LBBB, hyperkalemia, Brugada.

flashcards.question: When to record the first 12-lead
flashcards.answer: Within 10 minutes of reaching a chest pain patient; repeat when symptoms change.

flashcards.question: Wellens' T waves
flashcards.answer: Deep or biphasic T waves in V2–V3 after pain: critical LAD narrowing. High risk.

critical.scenario: A 55-year-old has chest pressure for 90 minutes. BP 146/90. ST elevation of 3 mm in II, III and aVF with ST depression in I and aVL. He has a true aspirin allergy (hives and wheeze).
critical.question: Territory, complication and the allergy?

options.t: Inferior STEMI: expect bradycardia and hypotension, record V4R; no aspirin – tell the PCI team about the allergy

options.f: This is inferior; and the allergy rules out aspirin by any route.

options.t: Inferior STEMI: give enteric-coated aspirin instead
options.f: Enteric coating doesn't prevent an allergic reaction.

options.t: Not a STEMI because of the reciprocal changes

critical.explanation: The hospital chooses another antiplatelet. Pre-notify the PCI centre and avoid nitrates until V4R rules out RV infarction.
critical.kpi: Inferior STEMI recognition and RV involvement

critical.scenario: A healthy 42-year-old has sharp chest pain that's worse lying flat and better leaning forward, 10 days after a cold. Diffuse concave ST elevation, PR depression, no reciprocal changes. The machine reads "***ACUTE MI***".
critical.question: Most likely diagnosis and action?

options.t: Pericarditis, a STEMI mimic: share your suspicion, transport for assessment
options.f: Correct. Don't trust the machine's label alone.
Diffuse changes with PR depression and positional pain point to pericarditis.
She still needs assessment to exclude MI.
No peaked T waves or wide QRS.

critical.explanation: STEMI is regional with reciprocal change; pericarditis is diffuse with PR depression. When unsure, transmit the ECG.

critical.scenario: A 60-year-old has crushing chest pain. The 12-lead shows 2 mm ST depression in V1–V3 and tall R waves in V2, nothing else.
critical.question: What should you do?

options.t: Record V7–V9: elevation there means a posterior STEMI, so pre-notify the PCI centre

options.f: Isolated V1–V3 depression may be a posterior STEMI.

options.t: Ignore: depression is never an emergency
options.f: It can be the mirror of a posterior STEMI.

critical.explanation: In V7–V9, 0.5 mm of ST elevation is enough.
critical.kpi: Recognizes a posterior STEMI from anterior ST depression and records posterior leads
